--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'Correct the reason for the logging bootstrap: the swift-log default handler writes to stderr, not stdout'
+---
+## What
+
+Four files give a false reason for the logging bootstrap in `acp-client`. They say that the default handler of swift-log writes to standard output. That is not true. `.build/checkouts/swift-log/Sources/Logging/LoggingSystem.swift` sets the default factory to `StreamLogHandler.standardError(label: label)`. The error came from rule 6 of the OpenTelemetry design of 2026-09-28; its author (session swissarmyhammer-05) corrected it on 2026-09-28.
+
+The code is still correct. The bootstrap is still necessary, but for a different reason: `cli-plan.md` §8 gives standard error to the terminal layer (`TerminalOutput`), and unrequested swift-log lines from the default handler would mix with that output. Standard output must still hold the answer text alone. Change only the text that gives the reason. Do not change behaviour.
+
+Text to correct:
+- [ ] `Sources/acp-client/TelemetryBootstrap.swift`: the doc comment of `TelemetryBootstrap`. Line 11–13 ("because the default handler of swift-log writes to standard output, and `cli-plan.md` §8 keeps standard output for the answer text alone"), line 16 ("never with a handler that writes to standard output"; keep the rule, it is still true, but also say it must not write to stderr outside the terminal layer), and line 29 ("which leaves the swift-log default on standard output" → on standard error, where the terminal layer owns the output).
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientTests/Telemetry/TelemetryBootstrapSourceTests.swift`: the suite doc comment, lines 7–10 (same false reason). A log record written before the bootstrap goes to standard error and mixes with the terminal layer.
+- [ ] `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientIntegrationTests/TelemetryBootstrapTests.swift`: the file comment, lines 5–10 ("The default handler of swift-log writes to standard output ..."). Say that the tests check both descriptors: stdout holds the answer alone, and stderr holds no log line that the terminal layer did not write. Keep the test names; their assertions (stdout holds the answer alone, stderr holds nothing) are still correct.
+- [ ] `cli-plan.md` §12, lines 450–451 ("because the default handler of swift-log writes to stdout, and §8 keeps stdout for the answer text. It never uses a handler that writes to stdout").
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] No comment, doc comment or `cli-plan.md` text in this package says that the swift-log default handler writes to standard output (check: `rg -n -i "swift-log.*(stdout|standard output)|default handler.*(stdout|standard output)" Sources Tests IntegrationTests/Tests cli-plan.md` gives no hit).
+- [ ] The new text names standard error and the terminal layer as the reason, in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
+- [ ] No production code changes; `git diff --stat` shows only comment and doc lines.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] No new test: the change is comments and documentation only. The existing tests prove that the behaviour did not change.
+- [ ] `swift test --parallel` passes (257 tests on 2026-09-29).
+- [ ] `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests` passes (103 tests on 2026-09-29).
+- [ ] The `rg` command in the acceptance criteria gives no hit.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. (Here: run the `rg` check first and see the 4 hits, then correct the text, then see 0 hits.)
+- Do not run `swift format`. #otel
\ No newline at end of file
